newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond primary mart quiet, awaits Fed.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond primary mart quiet, awaits Fed.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond players are are expected to stay on the sidelines awaiting the highly anticipated outcome of this week's meeting of Federal Reserve policy makers later Wednesday, dealers said.
"It's very quiet...people are just waiting for the outcome of today's FOMC meeting," said one high-grade syndicate source.

The policy-making arm of the Fed, the Federal Open Market Committee, is expected to issue a statement that the meeting has ended around 1415 EST/1915 GMT. The market widely anticipated the Fed would leave interest rates unchanged.

Philip Morris' $500 million A2/single-A rated notes, which priced as 7.20s to yield 7.343 percent, came at 78 basis points over the Treasury curve compared with talk in the range of 76 to 78 basis points.
Sherwin-Williams issued $700 million A2/single-A debt in a five-part public and private offering which traders called "attractively priced."
The public debt was priced at yields ranging from 25 basis points over Treasuries in three years to 63 basis points over the T-bond for 30-year debt.
